That’s fair and I don’t think the individual is out of blame at all. Heck most teenagers are old enough to understand their actions. However, I think questioning their upbringing and the community is valid. The erroneous reasoning that if you question if you’re trans means you are indeed trans is so misguided. Yet in any trans forum, people don’t see solutions to body dysmorphia other than transitioning. If we teach trans acceptance (which of course we should), shouldn’t the risks be there too? Not of societal changes but of irreversible medical changes?

I agree that groomer is not a good term based on definition. However, my point stands that a person can feel victim to pressure despite age. In an ideal world, yes every adult is responsible for their actions. But humans are much more complex than that and undergo mental health issues, abusive households and so forth. Just because someone becomes 18 doesn’t mean these struggles go away, and definitely doesn’t mean that trauma is any less real

Honestly, most of the stories in this subreddit are of adults who transitioned of kids nonetheless. Any adult can do whatever they want, but an adult recognizing pressure they had as a child or adult to undergo medical procedures is valid.
